title: T0
summary: We trained a 256M SOTA open-weights time-series forecasting model

extra.author: LTMeyer
extra.original_title: Show HN: T0: We trained a 256M SOTA open-weights time-series forecasting model

story_text.value:
Hi everyone, we are excited to share t0-gamma, the latest model in our t0 family. It is a 256M parameter open-weights foundation model for time series (TSFM). It runs on CPU, GPU or Apple chips.

https://huggingface.co/theforecastingcompany/t0-gamma

t0 leverages historical data to forecast the likely outcomes over a given horizon. It does so zero-shot. It works on almost any time series, as it can pick up small signals like trends and seasonality. It can also leverage future-known information, like holidays, promotions and weather forecasts. Under the hood, t0 is a transformer that alternates attention between time and across the variates of a series.

t0 is agnostic to the domain and to the frequency of the time series. For instance, it can be used to predict retail or electricity demand, as well as server metrics.

On European day ahead electricity prices, t0 reduces the error by a third compared with a naive baseline that repeats the previous day. Adding weather forecasts or holiday information improves it even further. There is a Colab notebook to try it. t0 has also been tested independently on electricity prices in Texas (ERCOT).

https://colab.research.google.com/github/theforecastingcompa...

Like other TSFMs, t0 outperforms classical techniques such as ARIMA, ETS and their variants. On the public benchmarks GIFT-Eval, fev-bench and TIME, t0-gamma currently ranks first among the other TSFMs. It means it is the most accurate model there is to date. Like other TSFMs, t0 can be used inside agentic, routing or ensembling systems. This can improve the scores on the leaderboards even further. Our tech report describes the model family and its evaluation.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24559

Trying it takes a few Python lines.

  pip install "tfc-t0[torch]>=0.6.0"

  from t0 import T0Forecaster
  model = T0Forecaster.from_pretrained("theforecastingcompany/t0-gamma").eval()
  history = ...  # history of the time series to predict
  out = model.predict(history, horizon=24)
  out.median
There is more to come. We are working to extend t0 to joint forecasts across related series and hierarchies, much longer contexts and faster inference.

Please give it a try, and don't hesitate to tell us where it works and where it doesn't.

We are The Forecasting Company. We want to help companies reduce their uncertainty about the future, so they can make better decisions. We are starting our journey by building foundation models for time series.

title: huggingface/transformers: Release v5.20.0
summary: # Release v5.20.0 ## New Model additions ### Muse Spark Open Muse Spark Open is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model from Meta that takes text, images, audio, and video as input and generates text. It has 816B total parameters (42B active per token) and a context window of up to 1,048,576 tokens shared across modalities. It is trained for agentic coding tasks such as multi-file editing, debugging, and tool use. Checkpoints are available in BF16 and NVFP4 formats. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/muse_spark) | [Blog Post](http://hf.co/blog/meta-muse-spark-open) * Add Muse Spark Open (#49644) by @guarin in [#49644](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49644) ### Ling 3.0 Ling 3.0 Flash is a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts language model from InclusionAI. Its decoder groups five Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) layers with one Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) layer. The MLA blocks use interleaved rotary embeddings and a head-wise output gate, and the feed-forward blocks combine routed and shared experts. It is natively supported in Transformers as `BailingHybridForCausalLM`, so it loads without `trust_remote_code=True`. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/bailing_hybrid) * [Model] Add native Ling 3.0 Flash support (#49446) by @icavan in [#49446](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49446) ### Kolibri1 Kolibri 1 is Aleph Alpha's mixture-of-experts reasoning model, focused on German and English. Each of its 50 layers routes every token to 6 of 384 experts using sigmoid routing, and adds one shared expert. Four sliding-window attention layers alternate with one full-attention layer, and RoPE is applied only in the sliding-window layers. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/kolibri1) * Add Kolibri 1 (#49463) by @lucamotz in [#49463](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49463) ### MiniCPM-V 4.7 [MiniCPM-V](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.18154) is a series of efficient multimodal large language models developed by [OpenBMB](https://github.com/OpenBMB). Like MiniCPM-V 4.6, the MiniCPM-V 4.7 architecture pairs a SigLIP vision encoder that has a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model backbone, and supports both 4x and 16x visual downsampling modes. The main addition over 4.6 is *canvas M-RoPE*: instead of numbering visual tokens along a single 1-D sequence, the model lays every image out on a 2-D canvas and assigns each visual token a `(temporal, height, width)` position, so slices of the same image keep their spatial relationship and video frames keep their temporal order. * Fix more stuff (#48979) by @zucchini-nlp in [#48979](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48979#top) ### UnlimitedOcr UnlimitedOcr is a single 3B-parameter OCR model from Baidu with a standard 32,768-token context length. It builds on DeepSeek OCR and replaces all decoder attention layers with Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA). This keeps the KV cache constant during decoding, so the model can transcribe dozens of pages in a single forward pass. It supports "gundam" mode (640x640 tiles with dynamic cropping) and "base" mode (a single 1024x1024 view), and it can output region detections with bounding boxes. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/unlimited_ocr) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2606.23050 (the docs link only the Hugging Face papers page, "Unlock OCR Works" is not given an arXiv link, so this is the paper URL provided)) * Add Unlimited OCR (#46836) by @guarin in [#46836](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/46836) ### UltraBERT UltraBERT is a family of bidirectional text encoders trained with a combination of masking ratios, pruning, and distillation for classification and retrieval tasks. The released encoders support sequences of up to 32,768 tokens. They use rotary position embeddings, RMSNorm, SwiGLU feed-forward layers, and alternating local and global attention (every third layer is global). Checkpoints include UltraBERT-150M and UltraBERT-380M for masked language modeling and fine-tuning, and UltraBERT-Embed-150M for text embeddings. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/ultrabert) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.15028) * Integrate the UltraBERT architecture (#49596) by @tomaarsen in [#49596](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49596) ### MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B is an end-to-end audio understanding model for long-form multi-speaker transcription, speaker diarization, and timestamps. It combines a Whisper-style encoder, a 4× frame merge step, a multi-modal projector, and a Qwen3 language model. It produces joint transcription and diarization in a single pass, with segments formatted as `[start][S01]text[end]`. It supports long-form audio through Whisper-window chunking in the processor, promptable transcription with hotword biasing, and 50+ languages. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/moss_transcribe_diarize) * Add MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize model (#48386) by @itazap in [#48386](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48386) ## Breaking changes 🚨 General breaking notice that inference with EP has regressions in speed; we are working on fixing this ASAP! 🚨 Deprecated checks and methods have been removed from `cache_utils.py` (affecting models such as minimax_m3_vl and pi0), so any code still calling those deprecated cache methods must switch to the current cache API. * 🚨 Remove deprecated cache utils methods (#49605) by @guarin Accidental imports from other models were removed from several model files (e.g. embedding_gemma2, ijepa, lightglue), and the modular converter now avoids adding such cross-model imports. If you imported these names through those model modules, import them from their original modules instead. * 🚨 Remove imports from other models (#49473) by @guarin The minimum `kernels` version is now 0.17.2, which allows `use_fallback=KernelizeFallback.ALL` so that a failed kernel load falls back to the original implementation instead of raising an error. Upgrade `kernels` to 0.17.2 or later. * 🚨 Bump min kernels to 0.17.2 for better fallback (#49235) by @SunMarc A new `SubConfigSpec` centralizes the initialization of sub-configs, so default sub-configs are collected from dataclass fields instead of by instantiating the class, and this touches the configuration utilities and many model configs. Custom or existing nested configs may need to be updated to declare their sub-configs through this mechanism. * :rotating_light: SubConfigSpec for centralized init of subconfigs (#48282) by @zucchini-nlp The LUKE and mLUKE tokenizers now treat entity special tokens such as `` as special tokens (not split, honored by `skip_special_tokens`, normalized) while keeping the same spacing as regular vocabulary tokens when decoding. Tokenization and decoding output involving these tokens may therefore differ from before, so check any code or saved outputs that depend on the old behavior. * 🚨🚨🚨 luke fixe (#48408) by @itazap ## Exporters Transformers exporters now support quantization directly during export across Dynamo, ONNX, OpenVINO, and ExecuTorch. The new unified quantization API integrates PT2E, ONNX Runtime, and NNCF quantizers, enabling static and dynamic quantization as well as weight-only compression (INT8/INT4), with configurable calibration workflows. This makes it easier to export optimized models for efficient inference across different backends. For more information see the docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/exporters_quantization ## Parallelization This release improves distributed training and inference. FSDP × TP model and optimizer checkpoints can now be saved and loaded across different parallel configurations, and expert-parallel dispatch, tensor-parallel plans, static-cache `generate()`, and the caching allocator's byte count were fixed. Tied LM heads in composite models now get their own TP plan entry, `enable_expert_parallel` applies the EP plan alone again, TPU loading uses the `tor * FSDP x TP Saving / Loading, Optimizer (#49256) by @michaelbenayoun in [#49256] * FSDP x TP Saving / Loading (#48802) by @michaelbenayoun in [#48802] * Don't set a device per rank for gloo tensor-parallel tests (#49636) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49636] * fix(distributed): keep enable_expert_parallel as EP alone (#49633) by @dacorvo in [#49633] * Fix a port allocation race in FSDP tests (#49455) by @icavan in [#49455] * Expert-parallel dispatch hands the experts the received rows, not the all-to-all's pending result (#49421) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49421] * Fix static-cache generate() with host-side inputs and under TP (#49317) by @dacorvo in [#49317] * Composite lm head tp plan (#49080) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49080] * Fix: use torch.accelerator device APIs so TP loading works again on TPU (#49502) by @tengomucho in [#49502] * Count ep and fsdp in caching_allocator_warmup byte calculation (#49384) by @3outeille in [#49384] * Do not wrap the model in FSDP for expert-parallel token dispatch (#49383) by @3outeille in [#49383] ## Generation This release fixes static-cache `generate()` bugs with host-side inputs and under tensor parallelism. It also speeds up Whisper generation on TPU by cutting device syncs and recompilation, and fixes Whisper batched timestamp decoding for tensor and NumPy inputs. Pipelines get a cleanup of generation-argument handling that removes spurious warnings. * Add job to automatically generate Intel CPU Docker image (#49560) by @regisss in [#49560] * Image decoding moves to torchcodec (#47963) by @zucchini-nlp in [#47963] * Optimize Whisper generation for TPU and device sync (#49426) by @tengomucho in [#49426] * Generation cleanup in pipelines (#49269) by @Rocketknight1 in [#49269] * Fix Whisper batch timestamp decoding for tensors (#49419) by @Kingofbooks in [#49419] ## Vision Vision processing was updated in several places. Image decoding now uses torchcodec, Molmo2's image and video kwargs follow the library's standard conventions, and Pixtral Flash Attention no longer detects false image boundaries after the axial RoPE refactor, which had caused CUDA illegal memory access errors and incorrect output. Several CI and Docker changes also shipped: GPU images moved to Python 3.11, a numpy/pyarrow conflict * Fix numpy/pyarrow conflict in the XPU Docker image (#49582) by @jiqing-feng in [#49582] * CI: Move GPU images to python 3.11 (#49352) by @tarekziade in [#49352] * Update molmo2 processing images/videos kwargs (#49563) by @guarin in [#49563] * Fix Pixtral Flash Attention image boundaries after axial RoPE refactor (#49373) by @oliverholworthy in [#49373] ## Kernels This release improves kernel support across hardware. `flash_attention_2` now falls back to the AITER kernel on ROCm when `flash-attn` isn't installed, and T5-style models get a contiguous SDPA position-bias mask so they use fused kernels again. The Hub rotary kernel is now limited to CUDA inference because its backward pass gave incorrect gradients. The Atlas Inference Gated DeltaNet kernels for Strix Halo and * Fall back to the AITER kernel for flash_attention_2 on ROCm (#49608) by @Abdennacer-Badaoui in [#49608] * Make the SDPA position_bias mask contiguous so T5-style models use fused kernels (#49517) by @IvenHsu01 in [#49517] * Use the Hub rotary kernel for inference only on CUDA (#49439) by @qgallouedec in [#49439] * [Atlas Inference] Enable torch.compile for the Strix Halo Gated DeltaNet hub kernel (#49453) by @AzeezIsh in [#49453] * [Atlas Inference] Fix GB10 Gated DeltaNet hub kernel for transformers 5.17+ and enable torch.compile (#49452) by @AzeezIsh in [#49452] ## Cache This release fixes several cache-related bugs: static-cache `generate()` now handles host-side nested inputs and tensor parallelism correctly, the offloaded cache prefetch no longer races with the offloading copy, and Phi3 LongRoPE cache rebuilds at the context boundary now receive the full prefix. It also counts the query token in MiMo-V2-Flash's sliding window and corrects the quantized cache (hqq/quanto) documentation exam * Fix offloaded cache prefetch racing with the offloading copy (#49363) by @qgallouedec in [#49363] * docs: update quantized cache hqq/quanto examples and documentation (#47212) by @DavidJohnQuinlan in [#47212] * [MiMo-V2-Flash] Count the query token in the sliding window (#49170) by @guapisolo in [#49170] * Fix Phi3 LongRoPE cache rebuild at the context boundary (#49361) by @LE0-Lin in [#49361] ## Bugfixes and improvements * [docs] Hardware docs payload.body: # Release v5.20.0 ## New Model additions ### Muse Spark Open Muse Spark Open is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model from Meta that takes text, images, audio, and video as input and generates text. It has 816B total parameters (42B active per token) and a context window of up to 1,048,576 tokens shared across modalities. It is trained for agentic coding tasks such as multi-file editing, debugging, and tool use. Checkpoints are available in BF16 and NVFP4 formats. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/muse_spark) | [Blog Post](http://hf.co/blog/meta-muse-spark-open) * Add Muse Spark Open (#49644) by @guarin in [#49644](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49644) ### Ling 3.0 Ling 3.0 Flash is a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts language model from InclusionAI. Its decoder groups five Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) layers with one Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) layer. The MLA blocks use interleaved rotary embeddings and a head-wise output gate, and the feed-forward blocks combine routed and shared experts. It is natively supported in Transformers as `BailingHybridForCausalLM`, so it loads without `trust_remote_code=True`. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/bailing_hybrid) * [Model] Add native Ling 3.0 Flash support (#49446) by @icavan in [#49446](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49446) ### Kolibri1 Kolibri 1 is Aleph Alpha's mixture-of-experts reasoning model, focused on German and English. Each of its 50 layers routes every token to 6 of 384 experts using sigmoid routing, and adds one shared expert. Four sliding-window attention layers alternate with one full-attention layer, and RoPE is applied only in the sliding-window layers. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/kolibri1) * Add Kolibri 1 (#49463) by @lucamotz in [#49463](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49463) ### MiniCPM-V 4.7 [MiniCPM-V](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.18154) is a series of efficient multimodal large language models developed by [OpenBMB](https://github.com/OpenBMB). Like MiniCPM-V 4.6, the MiniCPM-V 4.7 architecture pairs a SigLIP vision encoder that has a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model backbone, and supports both 4x and 16x visual downsampling modes. The main addition over 4.6 is *canvas M-RoPE*: instead of numbering visual tokens along a single 1-D sequence, the model lays every image out on a 2-D canvas and assigns each visual token a `(temporal, height, width)` position, so slices of the same image keep their spatial relationship and video frames keep their temporal order. * Fix more stuff (#48979) by @zucchini-nlp in [#48979](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48979#top) ### UnlimitedOcr UnlimitedOcr is a single 3B-parameter OCR model from Baidu with a standard 32,768-token context length. It builds on DeepSeek OCR and replaces all decoder attention layers with Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA). This keeps the KV cache constant during decoding, so the model can transcribe dozens of pages in a single forward pass. It supports "gundam" mode (640x640 tiles with dynamic cropping) and "base" mode (a single 1024x1024 view), and it can output region detections with bounding boxes. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/unlimited_ocr) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2606.23050 (the docs link only the Hugging Face papers page, "Unlock OCR Works" is not given an arXiv link, so this is the paper URL provided)) * Add Unlimited OCR (#46836) by @guarin in [#46836](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/46836) ### UltraBERT UltraBERT is a family of bidirectional text encoders trained with a combination of masking ratios, pruning, and distillation for classification and retrieval tasks. The released encoders support sequences of up to 32,768 tokens. They use rotary position embeddings, RMSNorm, SwiGLU feed-forward layers, and alternating local and global attention (every third layer is global). Checkpoints include UltraBERT-150M and UltraBERT-380M for masked language modeling and fine-tuning, and UltraBERT-Embed-150M for text embeddings. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/ultrabert) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.15028) * Integrate the UltraBERT architecture (#49596) by @tomaarsen in [#49596](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49596) ### MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B is an end-to-end audio understanding model for long-form multi-speaker transcription, speaker diarization, and timestamps. It combines a Whisper-style encoder, a 4× frame merge step, a multi-modal projector, and a Qwen3 language model. It produces joint transcription and diarization in a single pass, with segments formatted as `[start][S01]text[end]`. It supports long-form audio through Whisper-window chunking in the processor, promptable transcription with hotword biasing, and 50+ languages. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/moss_transcribe_diarize) * Add MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize model (#48386) by @itazap in [#48386](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48386) ## Breaking changes 🚨 General breaking notice that inference with EP has regressions in speed; we are working on fixing this ASAP! 🚨 Deprecated checks and methods have been removed from `cache_utils.py` (affecting models such as minimax_m3_vl and pi0), so any code still calling those deprecated cache methods must switch to the current cache API. * 🚨 Remove deprecated cache utils methods (#49605) by @guarin Accidental imports from other models were removed from several model files (e.g. embedding_gemma2, ijepa, lightglue), and the modular converter now avoids adding such cross-model imports. If you imported these names through those model modules, import them from their original modules instead. * 🚨 Remove imports from other models (#49473) by @guarin The minimum `kernels` version is now 0.17.2, which allows `use_fallback=KernelizeFallback.ALL` so that a failed kernel load falls back to the original implementation instead of raising an error. Upgrade `kernels` to 0.17.2 or later. * 🚨 Bump min kernels to 0.17.2 for better fallback (#49235) by @SunMarc A new `SubConfigSpec` centralizes the initialization of sub-configs, so default sub-configs are collected from dataclass fields instead of by instantiating the class, and this touches the configuration utilities and many model configs. Custom or existing nested configs may need to be updated to declare their sub-configs through this mechanism. * :rotating_light: SubConfigSpec for centralized init of subconfigs (#48282) by @zucchini-nlp The LUKE and mLUKE tokenizers now treat entity special tokens such as `` as special tokens (not split, honored by `skip_special_tokens`, normalized) while keeping the same spacing as regular vocabulary tokens when decoding. Tokenization and decoding output involving these tokens may therefore differ from before, so check any code or saved outputs that depend on the old behavior. * 🚨🚨🚨 luke fixe (#48408) by @itazap ## Exporters Transformers exporters now support quantization directly during export across Dynamo, ONNX, OpenVINO, and ExecuTorch. The new unified quantization API integrates PT2E, ONNX Runtime, and NNCF quantizers, enabling static and dynamic quantization as well as weight-only compression (INT8/INT4), with configurable calibration workflows. This makes it easier to export optimized models for efficient inference across different backends. For more information see the docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/exporters_quantization ## Parallelization This release improves distributed training and inference. FSDP × TP model and optimizer checkpoints can now be saved and loaded across different parallel configurations, and expert-parallel dispatch, tensor-parallel plans, static-cache `generate()`, and the caching allocator's byte count were fixed. Tied LM heads in composite models now get their own TP plan entry, `enable_expert_parallel` applies the EP plan alone again, TPU loading uses the `tor * FSDP x TP Saving / Loading, Optimizer (#49256) by @michaelbenayoun in [#49256] * FSDP x TP Saving / Loading (#48802) by @michaelbenayoun in [#48802] * Don't set a device per rank for gloo tensor-parallel tests (#49636) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49636] * fix(distributed): keep enable_expert_parallel as EP alone (#49633) by @dacorvo in [#49633] * Fix a port allocation race in FSDP tests (#49455) by @icavan in [#49455] * Expert-parallel dispatch hands the experts the received rows, not the all-to-all's pending result (#49421) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49421] * Fix static-cache generate() with host-side inputs and under TP (#49317) by @dacorvo in [#49317] * Composite lm head tp plan (#49080) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49080] * Fix: use torch.accelerator device APIs so TP loading works again on TPU (#49502) by @tengomucho in [#49502] * Count ep and fsdp in caching_allocator_warmup byte calculation (#49384) by @3outeille in [#49384] * Do not wrap the model in FSDP for expert-parallel token dispatch (#49383) by @3outeille in [#49383] ## Generation This release fixes static-cache `generate()` bugs with host-side inputs and under tensor parallelism. It also speeds up Whisper generation on TPU by cutting device syncs and recompilation, and fixes Whisper batched timestamp decoding for tensor and NumPy inputs. Pipelines get a cleanup of generation-argument handling that removes spurious warnings. * Add job to automatically generate Intel CPU Docker image (#49560) by @regisss in [#49560] * Image decoding moves to torchcodec (#47963) by @zucchini-nlp in [#47963] * Optimize Whisper generation for TPU and device sync (#49426) by @tengomucho in [#49426] * Generation cleanup in pipelines (#49269) by @Rocketknight1 in [#49269] * Fix Whisper batch timestamp decoding for tensors (#49419) by @Kingofbooks in [#49419] ## Vision Vision processing was updated in several places. Image decoding now uses torchcodec, Molmo2's image and video kwargs follow the library's standard conventions, and Pixtral Flash Attention no longer detects false image boundaries after the axial RoPE refactor, which had caused CUDA illegal memory access errors and incorrect output. Several CI and Docker changes also shipped: GPU images moved to Python 3.11, a numpy/pyarrow conflict * Fix numpy/pyarrow conflict in the XPU Docker image (#49582) by @jiqing-feng in [#49582] * CI: Move GPU images to python 3.11 (#49352) by @tarekziade in [#49352] * Update molmo2 processing images/videos kwargs (#49563) by @guarin in [#49563] * Fix Pixtral Flash Attention image boundaries after axial RoPE refactor (#49373) by @oliverholworthy in [#49373] ## Kernels This release improves kernel support across hardware. `flash_attention_2` now falls back to the AITER kernel on ROCm when `flash-attn` isn't installed, and T5-style models get a contiguous SDPA position-bias mask so they use fused kernels again. The Hub rotary kernel is now limited to CUDA inference because its backward pass gave incorrect gradients. The Atlas Inference Gated DeltaNet kernels for Strix Halo and * Fall back to the AITER kernel for flash_attention_2 on ROCm (#49608) by @Abdennacer-Badaoui in [#49608] * Make the SDPA position_bias mask contiguous so T5-style models use fused kernels (#49517) by @IvenHsu01 in [#49517] * Use the Hub rotary kernel for inference only on CUDA (#49439) by @qgallouedec in [#49439] * [Atlas Inference] Enable torch.compile for the Strix Halo Gated DeltaNet hub kernel (#49453) by @AzeezIsh in [#49453] * [Atlas Inference] Fix GB10 Gated DeltaNet hub kernel for transformers 5.17+ and enable torch.compile (#49452) by @AzeezIsh in [#49452] ## Cache This release fixes several cache-related bugs: static-cache `generate()` now handles host-side nested inputs and tensor parallelism correctly, the offloaded cache prefetch no longer races with the offloading copy, and Phi3 LongRoPE cache rebuilds at the context boundary now receive the full prefix. It also counts the query token in MiMo-V2-Flash's sliding window and corrects the quantized cache (hqq/quanto) documentation exam * Fix offloaded cache prefetch racing with the offloading copy title: ollama/ollama: v0.40.5
summary:
## NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super

[NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super](https://ollama.com/library/nemotron-3.5-super) is a vision-language model for coding, reasoning, tool use, and document understanding. It pairs a 120B-parameter hybrid Mamba-2/Transformer mixture-of-experts backbone (12B active per token) with a C-RADIO vision encoder, and supports tool calling, an on/off thinking mode, and context up to 1M tokens.

```
ollama run nemotron-3.5-super
```

A compact sibling, [Nemotron 3.5 Bolt](https://ollama.com/library/nemotron-3.5-bolt), distills Super down to 74B parameters (9B active) tuned to fit a 24 GB NVIDIA GPU for everyday agentic tasks, with speculative decoding via its included drafter.

## What's Changed
* Decision models are now available on cloud — use `clef:cloud` and `clef-flash:cloud` to run decision models through ollama.com cloud without pulling them locally
* Continuing an OpenAI-compatible Responses conversation that includes custom tool calls no longer fails with an error
* Clearer error messages when cloud access fails: sign-in problems, payment issues in the desktop app, and upstream access errors from the ChatGPT gateway now explain what went wrong
* Updated llama.cpp (adding Nemotron 3.5 support) and MLX

## New Contributors
* @willietran made their first contribution in https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/18986

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.4...v0.40.5

title: ggerganov/llama.cpp: v0.7.0
summary:
## Overview

llama.cpp v0.7.0 adds the LiliCorr speculative decoding technique and MTP for GLM5-Next, a new GPU cache for MoE experts kept in host memory (`--moe-cache-mib`, up to ~2.2x decode speedup when experts are offloaded), and a large batch of new models: K2 Horizon (dense and MoVA), Prism Bonsai 2 27B, EmbeddingGemma-2 (text+vision+audio), the LiquidAI d1/d1-omni and vLLM decision 2/d3 decision models, pplx-decider, MiniCPM-V 4.7, Nemotron Super 3.5 VL / Nemotron Bolt and maion-coder. The server gets a refactored chat session API (`common_chat_session`, part-based formatted output), much better slot and prompt-cache restore behavior, decision-model support for the new architectures and a new default port (9931), the web UI gains a full models manager, and ggml is updated to v0.27.0.

### Highlights

- New GPU cache for host-memory MoE experts (`--moe-cache-mib`): experts run on the GPU from an LRU cache, up to 2.2x faster decode [#29887](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29887)
- The expert cache is now shared across multiple GPUs [#30112](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30112)
- LiliCorr speculative decoding: candidate selection with a small draft transformer on top of DFlash [#30506](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30506)
- GLM5-Next: MTP speculative decoding with an optimized sparse attention path [#29928](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29928)
- K2 Horizon support in both dense and MoVA variants: conversion, tokenizer, chat template, `-sm tensor` splitting [#29535](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29535)
- Prism Bonsai 2 27B ternary model support [#29600](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29600)
- EmbeddingGemma-2: text + vision + audio embedding model [#30054](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30054)
- New decision models: LiquidAI d1-3B, d1-omni-600M, vLLM decision 2, vLLM d3 and pplx-decider [#30110](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30110) [#30114](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30114) [#30378](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30378) [#30383](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30383) [#30044](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30044)
- PLaMo-3 tokenizer implements reference pre-segmentation for exact tokenization parity [#30045](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30045)
- RPC server supports `-sm tensor` (tensor-parallel RPC, RPC protocol v8) [#26610](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26610)
- Server now listens on port 9931 by default instead of 8080 [#30159](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30159)

### API changes

- `include/llama.h`: new `moe_cache_size` context param for the host-expert GPU cache [#29887](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29887)
- `include/llama.h`: new `LLAMA_VOCAB_TYPE_PLAMO3` vocab type [#30045](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30045)
- `include/llama.h`: `llama_perf_context_data` reports graph reallocations during inference [#30329](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30329)
- `include/llama.h`: `embeddings` now skips the LM head when a pooling type other than NONE is used [#30445](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30445)
- `include/llama.h`: `llama_batch_ext_set_embd_state` returns false when the context has no state embedding, M-RoPE order documented [#30506](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30506)
- `tools/server`: chat layer refactored around `common_chat_session` with `feed()` / `finish()` [#30210](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30210)
- `tools/server`: formatted chat output is now an array of parts instead of a single string [#30389](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30389)
- `tools/server`: default listening port changed to 9931 (Docker images keep 8080 inside the container) [#30159](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30159)

### New models

- K2 Horizon: dense and MoVA variants with conversion, tokenizer, chat template and `-sm tensor` support [#29535](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29535)
- Prism Bonsai 2 27B (ternary) [#29600](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29600)
- EmbeddingGemma-2: text + vision + audio embeddings [#30054](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30054)
- LiquidAI d1-3B and d1-omni-600M decision models [#30110](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30110) [#30114](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30114)
- vLLM decision 2 and vLLM d3 models [#30378](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30378) [#30383](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30383)
- pplx-decider decision model [#30044](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30044)
- MiniCPM-V 4.7 multimodal model [#29416](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29416)
- Nemotron Super 3.5 VL and Nemotron Bolt 74B A9B [#30520](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30520)
- maion-coder architecture [#29778](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29778)
- Mellum: MoE gating parameters read from GGUF and unified RoPE handling [#30578](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30578)
- LiliCorr draft model conversion and graph [#30506](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30506)
- Rerankers: `classifier_activation` support, exact GELU for ModernBERT encoders [#29692](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29692) [#30108](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30108)

### Core changes

- Speculative decoding: MTP for GLM5-Next, LiliCorr drafts, correct mtmd handling in MTP graphs [#29928](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29928) [#30506](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30506) [#30257](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30257)
- Speculative decoding: shared nextn tensor flags with consolidated row cropping and sched re-reserve on flag change [#30097](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30097) [#30017](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30017) [#30020](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30020)
- Speculative decoding: fixed draft sampling and rejection handling, DFlash output head sharing [#30095](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30095) [#30111](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30111)
- New `--spec-draft-n-ubatch` to size the draft context batch separately and save VRAM [#30459](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30459)
- MoE expert cache: host-memory experts served from a device LRU cache, supported over multiple GPUs [#29887](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29887) [#30112](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30112)
- Embedding models: skip the logits buffer and the LM head when pooling is enabled (up to 10x less VRAM) [#30255](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30255) [#30445](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30445)
- Embedding graphs: reordered `get_rows`, dropped the redundant `t_embd` expand and leftover `ggml_cont` calls [#30160](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30160) [#30461](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30461) [#30198](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30198)
- No-cache attention: padded KV dimension and KQ bias, avoided graph reallocations [#30416](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30416) [#30446](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30446) [#30439](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30439)
- k-pool models: selection built in the causal mask layout, fixed a scatter data race on shared sequences [#30480](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30480) [#29994](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29994)
- GLM5-Next sparse attention: removed the gather path [#30042](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30042)
- KV cache: honor `LLAMA_STATE_SEQ_FLAGS_PARTIAL_ONLY` so draft checkpoints stop carrying the full KV [#30514](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30514)
- Prefetching: merge ranges before issuing system prefetch calls, never map foreign ranges into a backend buffer [#30532](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30532) [#30405](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30405)
- Sampling: greedy selection for eligible temperature-zero chains, backend sampling graph kept static across ubatches [#29797](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29797) [#30223](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30223)
- Tokenizers: PLaMo-3 pre-segmentation and FiM tokens, opt-in NFC normalization for Unigram, strict UTF-8 validation [#30045](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30045) [#30090](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30090) [#30390](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30390) [#30485](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30485)
- Jinja: fixed loop variable scoping, Python-compatible `tojson` rendering, faster context copy [#30533](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30533) [#30483](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30483) [#30362](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30362) [#30562](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30562)
- Model split: distribute layers evenly when no device reports free memory [#29677](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29677)

### Multi-modality changes

- Added `mtmd_build_inp_attn_mask` for building non-causal multimodal attention masks [#30259](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30259)
- Added cohere2 vision encoder support [#30062](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30062)
- MTP drafts now handle mtmd inputs, Qwen3.8 Flash Next accepts image embeddings [#30257](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30257) [#30397](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30397)
- New multimodal architectures: MiniCPM-V 4.7, Nemotron Super 3.5 VL, EmbeddingGemma-2 (vision + audio) [#29416](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29416) [#30520](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30520) [#30054](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30054)

### Server changes

- `/v1/systemone` extended to the new decision models: d1-3B, d1-omni, vLLM decision 2/d3, pplx-decider [#30110](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30110) [#30114](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30114) [#30378](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30378) [#30383](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30383) [#30044](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30044)
- Chat refactor: session-based parsing and part-based formatted output [#30210](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30210) [#30389](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30389)
- Generated text and tokens are now accumulated as parser input, preparing token-aware parsing [#29876](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29876)
- Prompt cache: only restorable slot states are saved, so rerank and embedding requests no longer fill the cache [#30498](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30498)
- Prompt cache: child tasks prefer empty slots and preserve the state they would overwrite [#30567](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30567)
- A pinned busy slot is left untouched until the request can run on it [#30295](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30295)
- Slot save/restore now keeps context checkpoints and the draft model state [#26004](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26004) [#30574](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30574)
- Fixed an off-by-two in the SWA reuse threshold that discarded restored states [#30580](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30580)
- Fixed a stack-overflow crash when escaping special tokens with `std::regex` [#30243](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30243)
- `LLAMA_ARG_SLOT_SAVE_PATH` environment variable for `--slot-save-path` [#30272](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30272)
- New per-component server tests; vendored cpp-httplib updated to 0.61.0 [#30312](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30312) [#30494](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30494) [#30134](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30134) [#30081](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30081)

### UI changes

- New Models Manager: one table of all served models with expandable quants, search, filters, sorting and favorites [#29583](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29583)
- Row actions: load/unload, delete from disk, hide/unhide, resumable downloads with progress [#29583](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29583)
- Model configuration side drawer with model info, chat template and "start a new chat" / "use in this chat" actions [#29583](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29583)
- Models manager follow-ups: GGUF training context, favorite UX, filter and sort fixes [#30228](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30228)
- Fixed `ui_settings` not being applied on the first visit in router mode [#29668](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29668)
- Fixed text attachment preview overflow for large pasted text [#29898](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29898)
- Fixed the default agentic turns limit falling back to 10 instead of 100 [#30582](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30582)

### ggml changes

- ggml updated to [v0.27.0](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/releases/tag/v0.27.0): the backend scheduler gains user callbacks for split weight copying and compute-buffer reallocation, and the RPC protocol is bumped to v8 for tensor-parallel RPC servers. Backends gained chunked gated-delta-net kernels on CUDA/HIP, KleidiAI SME2 k-quant matmuls and AVX2 Q2_0 dot products on CPU, L2-aware coopmat2 scheduling and bf16 activations on Vulkan, reordered-layout MoE kernels (MXFP4, IQ3, Q5_K, grouped XMX GEMM) on SYCL, dp4a MoE GEMMs on OpenCL, tensor-API and wider-head-dim flash attention on Metal, and a DMA/HVX copy overhaul with pooling and 3D im2col ops on Hexagon. Correctness work focused on non-contiguous and strided views, grid and workgroup size limits, out-of-bounds accesses and well-defined `mul_mat_id` behavior for duplicate expert ids; symbol visibility now defaults to hidden

payload.name: v0.7.0
payload.body:
## Overview

llama.cpp v0.7.0 adds the LiliCorr speculative decoding technique and MTP for GLM5-Next, a new GPU cache for MoE experts kept in host memory (`--moe-cache-mib`, up to ~2.2x decode speedup when experts are offloaded), and a large batch of new models: K2 Horizon (dense and MoVA), Prism Bonsai 2 27B, EmbeddingGemma-2 (text+vision+audio), the LiquidAI d1/d1-omni and vLLM decision 2/d3 decision models, pplx-decider, MiniCPM-V 4.7, Nemotron Super 3.5 VL / Nemotron Bolt and maion-coder. The server gets a refactored chat session API (`common_chat_session`, part-based formatted output), much better slot and prompt-cache restore behavior, decision-model support for the new architectures and a new default port (9931), the web UI gains a full models manager, and ggml is updated to v0.27.0.

### Highlights

- New GPU cache for host-memory MoE experts (`--moe-cache-mib`): experts run on the GPU from an LRU cache, up to 2.2x faster decode [#29887](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29887)
- The expert cache is now shared across multiple GPUs [#30112](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30112)
- LiliCorr speculative decoding: candidate selection with a small draft transformer on top of DFlash [#30506](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30506)
- GLM5-Next: MTP speculative decoding with an optimized sparse attention path [#29928](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29928)
- K2 Horizon support in both dense and MoVA variants: conversion, tokenizer, chat template, `-sm tensor` splitting [#29535](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29535)
- Prism Bonsai 2 27B ternary model support [#29600](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29600)
- EmbeddingGemma-2: text + vision + audio embedding model [#30054](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30054)
- New decision models: LiquidAI d1-3B, d1-omni-600M, vLLM decision 2, vLLM d3 and pplx-decider [#30110](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30110) [#30114](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30114) [#30378](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30378) [#30383](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30383) [#30044](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30044)
- PLaMo-3 tokenizer implements reference pre-segmentation for exact tokenization parity [#30045](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30045)
- RPC server supports `-sm tensor` (tensor-parallel RPC, RPC protocol v8) [#26610](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26610)
- Server now listens on port 9931 by default instead of 8080 [#30159](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30159)

### API changes

- `include/llama.h`: new `moe_cache_size` context param for the host-expert GPU cache [#29887](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29887)
- `include/llama.h`: new `LLAMA_VOCAB_TYPE_PLAMO3` vocab type [#30045](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30045)
- `include/llama.h`: `llama_perf_context_data` reports graph reallocations during inference [#30329](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30329)
- `include/llama.h`: `embeddings` now skips the LM head when a pooling type other than NONE is used [#30445](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30445)
- `include/llama.h`: `llama_batch_ext_set_embd_state` returns false when the context has no state embedding, M-RoPE order documented [#30506](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30506)
- `tools/server`: chat layer refactored around `common_chat_session` with `feed()` / `finish()` [#30210](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30210)
- `tools/server`: formatted chat output is now an array of parts instead of a single string [#30389](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30389)
- `tools/server`: default listening port changed to 9931 (Docker images keep 8080 inside the container) [#30159](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30159)

### New models

- K2 Horizon: dense and MoVA variants with conversion, tokenizer, chat template and `-sm tensor` support [#29535](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29535)
- Prism Bonsai 2 27B (ternary) [#29600](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29600)
- EmbeddingGemma-2: text + vision + audio embeddings [#30054](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30054)
- LiquidAI d1-3B and d1-omni-600M decision models [#30110](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30110) [#30114](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30114)
- vLLM decision 2 and vLLM d3 models [#30378](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30378) [#30383](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30383)
- pplx-decider decision model [#30044](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30044)
- MiniCPM-V 4.7 multimodal model [#29416](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29416)
- Nemotron Super 3.5 VL and Nemotron Bolt 74B A9B [#30520](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30520)
- maion-coder architecture [#29778](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29778)
- Mellum: MoE gating parameters read from GGUF and unified RoPE handling [#30578](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30578)
- LiliCorr draft model conversion and graph [#30506](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30506)
- Rerankers: `classifier_activation` support, exact GELU for ModernBERT encoders [#29692](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29692) [#30108](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30108)

### Core changes

- Speculative decoding: MTP for GLM5-Next, LiliCorr drafts, correct mtmd handling in MTP graphs [#29928](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29928) [#30506](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30506) [#30257](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30257)
- Speculative decoding: shared nextn tensor flags with consolidated row cropping and sched re-reserve on flag change [#30097](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30097) [#30017](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30017) [#30020](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30020)
- Speculative decoding: fixed draft sampling and rejection handling, DFlash output head sharing [#30095](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30095) [#30111](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30111)
- New `--spec-draft-n-ubatch` to size the draft context batch separately and save VRAM [#30459](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30459)
- MoE expert cache: host-memory experts served from a device LRU cache, supported over multiple GPUs [#29887](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29887) [#30112](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30112)
- Embedding models: skip the logits buffer and the LM head when pooling is enabled (up to 10x less VRAM) [#30255](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30255) [#30445](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30445)
- Embedding graphs: reordered `get_rows`, dropped the redundant `t_embd` expand and leftover `ggml_cont` calls [#30160](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30160) [#30461](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30461) [#30198](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30198)
- No-cache attention: padded KV dimension and KQ bias, avoided graph reallocations [#30416](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30416) [#30446](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30446) [#30439](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30439)
- k-pool models: selection built in the causal mask layout, fixed a scatter data race on shared sequences [#30480](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30480) [#29994](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29994)
- GLM5-Next sparse attention: removed the gather path [#30042](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30042)
- KV cache: honor `LLAMA_STATE_SEQ_FLAGS_PARTIAL_ONLY` so draft checkpoints stop carrying the full KV [#30514](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30514)
- Prefetching: merge ranges before issuing system prefetch calls, never map foreign ranges into a backend buffer [#30532](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30532) [#30405](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30405)
- Sampling: greedy selection for eligible temperature-zero chains, backend sampling graph kept static across ubatches [#29797](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29797) [#30223](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30223)
- Tokenizers: PLaMo-3 pre-segmentation and FiM tokens, opt-in NFC normalization for Unigram, strict UTF-8 validation [#30045](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30045) [#30090](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30090) [#30390](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30390) [#30485](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30485)
- Jinja: fixed loop variable scoping, Python-compatible `tojson` rendering, faster context copy [#30533](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30533) [#30483](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30483) [#30362](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30362) [#30562](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30562)
- Model split: distribute layers evenly when no device reports free memory [#29677](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29677)

### Multi-modality changes

- Added `mtmd_build_inp_attn_mask` for building non-causal multimodal attention masks [#30259](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30259)
- Added cohere2 vision encoder support [#30062](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30062)
- MTP drafts now handle mtmd inputs, Qwen3.8 Flash Next accepts image embeddings [#30257](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30257) [#30397](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30397)
- New multimodal architectures: MiniCPM-V 4.7, Nemotron Super 3.5 VL, EmbeddingGemma-2 (vision + audio) [#29416](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29416) [#30520](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30520) [#30054](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30054)

### Server changes

- `/v1/systemone` extended to the new decision models: d1-3B, d1-omni, vLLM decision 2/d3, pplx-decider [#30110](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30110) [#30114](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30114) [#30378](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30378) [#30383](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30383) [#30044](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30044)
- Chat refactor: session-based parsing and part-based formatted output [#30210](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30210) [#30389](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30389)
- Generated text and tokens are now accumulated as parser input, preparing token-aware parsing [#29876](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29876)
- Prompt cache: only restorable slot states are saved, so rerank and embedding requests no longer fill the cache [#30498](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30498)
- Prompt cache: child tasks prefer empty slots and preserve the state they would overwrite [#30567](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30567)
- A pinned busy slot is left untouched until the request can run on it [#30295](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30295)
- Slot save/restore now keeps context checkpoints and the draft model state [#26004](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26004) [#30574](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30574)
- Fixed an off-by-two in the SWA reuse threshold that discarded restored states [#30580](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30580)
- Fixed a stack-overflow crash when escaping special tokens with `std::regex` [#30243](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30243)
- `LLAMA_ARG_SLOT_SAVE_PATH` environment variable for `--slot-save-path` [#30272](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30272)
- New per-component server tests; vendored cpp-httplib updated to 0.61.0 [#30312](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30312) [#30494](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30494) [#30134](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30134) [#30081](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30081)

### UI changes

- New Models Manager: one table of all served models with expandable quants, search, filters, sorting and favorites [#29583](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29583)
- Row actions: load/unload, delete from disk, hide/unhide, resumable downloads with progress [#29583](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29583)
- Model configuration side drawer with model info, chat template and "start a new chat" / "use in this chat" actions [#29583](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29583)
- Models manager follow-ups: GGUF training context, favorite UX, filter and sort fixes [#30228](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30228)
- Fixed `ui_settings` not being applied on the first visit in router mode [#29668](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29668)
- Fixed text attachment preview overflow for large pasted text [#29898](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29898)
- Fixed the default agentic turns limit falling back to 10 instead of 100 [#30582](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30582)

### ggml changes

- ggml updated to [v0.27.0](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/releases/tag/v0.27.0): the backend scheduler gains user callbacks for split weight copying and compute-buffer reallocation, and the RPC protocol is bumped to v8 for tensor-parallel RPC servers. Backends gained chunked gated-delta-net kernels on CUDA/HIP, KleidiAI SME2 k-quant matmuls and AVX2 Q2_0 dot products on CPU, L2-aware coopmat2 scheduling and bf16 activations on Vulkan, reordered-layout MoE kernels (MXFP4, IQ3, Q5_K, grouped XMX GEMM) on SYCL, dp4a MoE GEMMs on OpenCL, tensor-API and wider-head-dim flash attention on Metal, and a DMA/HVX copy overhaul with pooling and 3D im2col ops on Hexagon. Correctness work focused on non-contiguous and strided views, grid and workgroup size limits, out-of-bounds accesses and well-defined `mul_mat_id` behavior for duplicate expert ids; symbol visibility now defaults to hidden

title: Trust in Depth: Giving agents more autonomy without losing control
summary: In every conversation I have with enterprise leaders, they say the same thing. They want agents to do more, but they don’t trust them to do it right all the time. That’s fair. The same creativity and autonomy that makes agents useful makes them hard to trust. Give an agent a task and it finds its own path to finish it, picking tools and sequencing steps no developer scripted. Run the same task twice and it might take a different route each time. A test that passes today tells you little about what the agent does tomorrow. The usual answer is a person in the loop, approving everything the agent does. That works at small scale, but as agents take on more work, human approvals pile up and review fatigue sets in. People asked to check everything stop catching the things that matter. Caution becomes a bottleneck, and agents capable of far more sit idle on the valuable work that could be making more of an impact. title: Build long-horizon agents with Grok 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock
summary: SpaceXAI’s Grok 4.7 is now available on Amazon Bedrock, which offers a choice of foundation models (FMs) from multiple providers. According to SpaceXAI, Grok 4.7 is trained to work longer on more difficult tasks and knows when to check its own work. That matters most for agents, which carry a task through many steps and must verify what they find along the way. An agent that works this way has to do more than look things up. It has to form a candidate answer, check it against what it has learned, and refine it until it fits. Grok 4.7 exposes a reasoning effort setting that controls how much deliberation happens before each response, and for agent workloads a practical question is which level to run. In this post, we build a tool-calling agent on Grok 4.7 and evaluate it on three tasks that require search rather than lookup. The tasks are diagnosing a two-service outage from its alerts, scheduling maintenance under interacting constraints, and choosing an optimal set of migrations under a budget. Each task has exactly one correct answer, verified by brute force. We ran all three at every reasoning effort level, six times each, for 72 agent runs.

title: Mixture-of-Experts kernel engineering on Amazon SageMaker AI
summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) is a sparsely-activated architecture that scales large language model (LLM) capacity while keeping per-token compute low. Because its operations account for a large share of total compute time, inefficiencies there directly raise request latency and cost. Therefore, optimizing MoE operations through kernel engineering offers the largest opportunity for performance gains. Fused MoE is a key optimization technique for the MoE architecture. A fused MoE system merges token routing, data shuffling, and specialized network calculations into a single batched operation on the GPU. This replaces executing those routing and expert computations as separate, sequential loop operations. While this provides latency advantages, it also brings complexity in kernel implementations and debugging capability. High GPU utilization for this architecture requires hardware-specific optimizations. In this post, we describe the different kernel optimizations we implemented for fused MoE models and show you how you can benefit from this work. We used a representative MoE model as our primary example. Swap-AB for WGMMA utilization To maximize tensor processing throughput, the NVIDIA Hopper architecture relies on the Warp Group Matrix Multiply Accumulate (WGMMA) instruction protocol, which executes collectively across a cooperative warpgroup of 128 threads.
